exposure: Mode of birth (sterile Caesarean-sectioned vs. nonsterile naturally born)
outcome: Antimicrobial activity of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF)
cohort: Newborn cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator knockout (CF) ferrets and non-CF control ferrets.
finding: Newborn CF ferrets exhibit defects in innate immunity and inflammatory signaling, including reduced airway surface liquid, impaired mucociliary clearance after 7 days, and selectively lower antimicrobial activity against Pseudomonas, which contributes to early lung disease.
mod_finding: During the birth transition, IL-8 was selectively induced in CF BALF in nonsterile naturally born animals compared to sterile Caesarean-sectioned, despite no genotypic difference in bacterial load shortly after birth.
